hints: Start from the left-hand side (LHS) and express $\tan^2\theta$ as $\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$.
Combine the two terms over a common denominator $\cos^2\theta$.
Use the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ in both numerator and denominator, and expand to show the RHS.
walkthrough:
Start from the Left-Hand Side (LHS) and use $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$:
$$\text{LHS} = 3\tan^2\theta + 5\sin^2\theta = 3\left(\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\right) + 5\sin^2\theta$$

Put over the common denominator $\cos^2\theta$ and apply $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{3\sin^2\theta + 5\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{3\sin^2\theta + 5\sin^2\theta(1 - \sin^2\theta)}{1 - \sin^2\theta}$$

Expand and simplify the numerator to complete the proof:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{3\sin^2\theta + 5\sin^2\theta - 5\sin^4\theta}{1 - \sin^2\theta} = \frac{8\sin^2\theta - 5\sin^4\theta}{1 - \sin^2\theta} \equiv \text{RHS}$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Uses $\tan^2\theta = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$, substitutes $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$, and completes algebraic proof to obtain $\frac{8\sin^2\theta-5\sin^4\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}$.

hints: Substitute the identity from part (a) into $3\tan^2\theta+5\sin^2\theta=9$, giving $\frac{8\sin^2\theta-5\sin^4\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta} = 9$.
Multiply across by $(1-\sin^2\theta)$ and rearrange into a quadratic in $\sin^2\theta$: $5\sin^4\theta - 17\sin^2\theta + 9 = 0$.
Solve using the quadratic formula for $\sin^2\theta$, discarding the root greater than 1.
Find the basic angle $\alpha = \arcsin(\sqrt{\sin^2\theta})$ and list all solutions in the interval $0^\circ < \theta < 270^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Use the identity from part (a) to rewrite the equation in terms of $\sin^2\theta$:
$$\frac{8\sin^2\theta - 5\sin^4\theta}{1 - \sin^2\theta} = 9 \implies 8\sin^2\theta - 5\sin^4\theta = 9 - 9\sin^2\theta$$

Rearrange into a 3-term quadratic in $\sin^2\theta$ and solve using the quadratic formula:
$$5\sin^4\theta - 17\sin^2\theta + 9 = 0 \implies \sin^2\theta = \frac{17 \pm \sqrt{17^2 - 4(5)(9)}}{2(5)} = \frac{17 \pm \sqrt{109}}{10}$$

Evaluate both roots (rejecting $\sin^2\theta > 1$) and take the square root:
$$\sin^2\theta = \frac{17 - \sqrt{109}}{10} \approx 0.65597 \implies \sin\theta = \pm 0.80992$$

Find the basic acute reference angle $\alpha$:
$$\alpha = \arcsin(0.80992) \approx 54.086^\circ$$

Calculate all angles within the domain $0^\circ < \theta < 270^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Quadrant 1: } & \theta = 54.1^\circ \\ \text{Quadrant 2: } & \theta = 180^\circ - 54.086^\circ = 125.9^\circ \\ \text{Quadrant 3: } & \theta = 180^\circ + 54.086^\circ = 234.1^\circ \end{aligned}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Forms quadratic $5\sin^4\theta - 17\sin^2\theta + 9 = 0$, finds $\sin^2\theta = \frac{17-\sqrt{109}}{10}$, and calculates angles $54.1^\circ, 125.9^\circ, 234.1^\circ$.
